import sys
import json

for line in sys.stdin:
    line = line.strip()
    if not line:
        continue
    try:
        obj = json.loads(line)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        print(json.dumps({"error": "invalid_content"}))
        continue

    if not isinstance(obj, dict):
        print(json.dumps({"error": "invalid_content"}))
        continue

    op = obj.get("op")
    title = obj.get("title")
    body = obj.get("body")

    if op != "render":
        print(json.dumps({"error": "invalid_content"}))
        continue

    if not isinstance(title, str) or not isinstance(body, str):
        print(json.dumps({"error": "invalid_content"}))
        continue

    print(json.dumps({"text": title + "\n" + body}))

goal:
Implement JSON-lines handler for {op:'render',title:string,body:string}. Return {text:title+'\n'+body}. Missing/non-string title or body returns {error:'invalid_content'}. Continue per line. Create main.py only, read JSON objects one per input line, print one JSON response per line and no other stdout. Implement exactly this public contract. Validate input strictly: a JSON value that is not an object is invalid; required fields must have the exact types named in the contract (booleans and numeric strings are not integers); reject invalid input with the contract's error response instead of raising. Return only the fields the contract defines.
An object that does not exactly match the operation shape is invalid: return only the contract's invalid response, with no additional fields. For a transition, include status only when from and to are strings and the operation is the specified transition.

Write exactly one file, main.py. Do not create tests, helper modules, or shell scripts.
